## Purpose

  Fix NaNs in ROCm prefix attention when DFlash2 uses sliding-window attention with a hybrid target model. #53323 

  Out-of-window positions can reference stale physical KV-cache blocks containing non-finite values. Masking those positions only after attention computation allows `0 * NaN` to propagate. This change masks block-table and K/V loads before they participate in attention math.

  A regression test covers stale nonzero block IDs containing NaNs.

  ## Test Plan

  ```bash
  pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py \
    -k sliding_window_masks_stale_nan_blocks
```

  ### DFlash2 with ROCm attention

    --served-model-name Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-ROCM-FIX \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --port 8016 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --max-model-len 65536 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 \
    --max-num-seqs 16 \

    --enable-chunked-prefill \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --async-scheduling \
    --generation-config vllm \
    --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
    --speculative-config \
    '{"method":"dflash","model":"/data/users/yzhen/models/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"ROCM_ATTN"}' \

nodes.body:
Additional kernel-level evidence and a decode counterpart to this prefix repair. The duplicate check also found #49588, so I am sharing the patch here for coordination rather than opening a competing PR.

There is a remaining partial-tile case beyond skipping whole expired blocks. With `seq_len=4352`, `sliding_window=4095` and physical/kernel block size32, live keys start at257. Token256 is expired but shares the first retained tile with live token257. Poisoning only token256 still produces NaNs with #49588's loop-start change, because that token's K/V are loaded before the score mask. Extending the existing decode load predicate to the window boundary prevents this.

Focused pytest results on an allocated AMD GPU (BF16, PyTorch2.11.0+gitd0c8b1f, ROCm7.2.53211, Triton3.6.0):

| Decode implementation | Whole expired page (8 cases) | Expired token in first retained tile (4 cases) |
|---|---|---|
| Stock decode at this PR's `aa93f64c` head | 8 poisoned-output assertion failures | 4 poisoned-output assertion failures |
| Exact #49588 diff (`0b1ffc75`) on that same source | 8 passed | 4 poisoned-output assertion failures |
| Load-mask patch below | 8 passed | 4 passed |

Every variant passed the clean-input FP64 comparison before poisoning. The unchanged bound is `atol=3e-4, rtol=3e-2`. Cases cover ordinary and padded cache strides, V-only and K+V NaNs, and null/nonzero whole-page IDs. Boundary poisoning uses direct indexed assignment so it modifies the actual cache, not an advanced-indexing copy. Full upstream conftests remained enabled, and the exact imported kernel/test hashes and per-case JUnit outcomes were checked. This is focused Python-kernel coverage on an older installed vLLM runtime, not model-evaluation or throughput qualification.

Command for the appended tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py \
  -k 'decode_sliding_window_ignores_stale_nan_pages or decode_sliding_window_ignores_expired_boundary_token' \
  -q --junitxml=decode-window.xml
```

The decode patch preserves the no-window path and existing score semantics. It can coexist with #49588's whole-block skip; the combined implementation has not been tested in this run. The prefix implementation remains owned by this PR.

<details><summary>Decode load-mask patch</summary>

```diff
--- a/vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py
+++ b/vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py
@@ -185,8 +185,16 @@
         # use the cheaper token-uniform dim_mask (matching the pre-0.25.0 fast
         # path) and skip the per-token predicate entirely.
         # K : (HEAD_SIZE, BLOCK_SIZE), V : (BLOCK_SIZE, HEAD_SIZE)
-        if j == num_blocks - 1:
+        # Retired sliding-window entries may contain nonfinite values.
+        # Mask their loads: a zero attention weight does not neutralize NaN.
+        if j == num_blocks - 1 or (
+            SLIDING_WINDOW > 0 and start_n < seq_len - SLIDING_WINDOW
+        ):
             kv_load_mask = abs_token_idx < seq_len
+            if SLIDING_WINDOW > 0:
+                kv_load_mask = kv_load_mask & (
+                    (seq_len - 1 - abs_token_idx) < SLIDING_WINDOW
+                )
             K_load = tl.load(
                 key_cache_ptr + k_offset,
                 mask=dim_mask[:, None] & kv_load_mask[None, :],
```
</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer patch against this PR's aa93f64c test file (12 focused cases)</summary>

```diff
--- a/tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py
+++ b/tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py
@@ -1137,3 +1137,186 @@
         device=device,
         op=op,
     )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("stale_page", [0, 1], ids=["null_page", "nonzero_page"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("padded_layout", [False, True], ids=["native", "hybrid_stride"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("nonfinite_keys", [False, True], ids=["value_nan", "key_value_nan"])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_decode_sliding_window_ignores_stale_nan_pages(
+    stale_page: int, padded_layout: bool, nonfinite_keys: bool,
+) -> None:
+    # Regression for a retired/null leading page containing NaN: masking its
+    # score does not prevent a zero attention weight times NaN value.
+    # Exercise only decode; prefix coverage belongs to upstream PR #53628.
+    # The window selects the Triton path without a vendor override.
+    device = CUDA_DEVICES[0]
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device)
+    set_random_seed(46236)
+    batch, hq, hkv, dim, block, packing = 32, 16, 2, 128, 32, 8
+    seq_len, window = 4352, 4095
+    dtype = torch.bfloat16
+    query_lens = [1] * batch
+    dense_k = (torch.randn(batch, seq_len, hkv, dim, device=device) * 0.1).to(dtype)
+    dense_v = (torch.randn_like(dense_k, dtype=torch.float32) * 0.1).to(dtype)
+    query = (torch.randn(sum(query_lens), hq, dim, device=device) * 0.1).to(dtype)
+    key = torch.cat([dense_k[r, -n:] for r, n in enumerate(query_lens)])
+    value = torch.cat([dense_v[r, -n:] for r, n in enumerate(query_lens)])
+    starts = [0]
+    for n in query_lens:
+        starts.append(starts[-1] + n)
+    query_start_loc = torch.tensor(starts, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    seq_lens = torch.full((batch,), seq_len, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    pages_per_req = seq_len // block
+    table = torch.arange(1, batch * pages_per_req + 1, device=device,
+                         dtype=torch.int32).reshape(batch, pages_per_req)
+    table[:, 0] = stale_page
+    num_pages = 1 + batch * pages_per_req
+    span = hkv * dim * block
+    stride = span * (2 if padded_layout else 1)
+    key_cache = torch.empty_strided(
+        (num_pages, hkv, dim // packing, block, packing),
+        (stride, dim * block, block * packing, packing, 1),
+        device=device, dtype=dtype)
+    value_cache = torch.empty_strided(
+        (num_pages, hkv, dim, block),
+        (stride, dim * block, block, 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)
+    key_cache[1:].copy_(
+        dense_k.reshape(batch, pages_per_req, block, hkv, dim)
+        .permute(0, 1, 3, 4, 2)
+        .reshape(batch * pages_per_req, hkv, dim // packing, packing, block)
+        .permute(0, 1, 2, 4, 3))
+    value_cache[1:].copy_(
+        dense_v.reshape(batch, pages_per_req, block, hkv, dim)
+        .permute(0, 1, 3, 4, 2)
+        .reshape(batch * pages_per_req, hkv, dim, block))
+    key_cache[stale_page].zero_()
+    value_cache[stale_page].zero_()
+    # Even the first query cannot see any entry of the shared page.
+    assert seq_len - max(query_lens) - (block - 1) >= window
+    scale = torch.ones((), device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
+
+    expected = []
+    for req, n in enumerate(query_lens):
+        q64 = query[starts[req]:starts[req + 1]].double().transpose(0, 1)
+        k64 = dense_k[req].double().transpose(0, 1).repeat_interleave(hq // hkv, 0)
+        v64 = dense_v[req].double().transpose(0, 1).repeat_interleave(hq // hkv, 0)
+        # Reuse the existing explicit causal/window mask helper; FP64 matmul
+        # and softmax are independent of the kernel under test.
+        mask = create_causal_attention_mask_for_sdpa(
+            [n], [seq_len], sliding_window=window,
+            device=torch.device(device), dtype=torch.float64)
+        scores = (q64 @ k64.transpose(1, 2)) * dim ** -0.5 + mask
+        expected.append((scores.softmax(-1) @ v64).transpose(0, 1))
+    expected_output = torch.cat(expected)
+
+    def attention() -> torch.Tensor:
+        output = torch.empty_like(query)
+        chunked_prefill_paged_decode(
+            query=query, key=key, value=value, output=output,
+            kv_cache_dtype="auto", key_cache=key_cache, value_cache=value_cache,
+            block_table=table, query_start_loc=query_start_loc, seq_lens=seq_lens,
+            max_seq_len=seq_len, max_query_len=max(query_lens),
+            k_scale=scale, v_scale=scale, sliding_window=window,
+            sm_scale=dim ** -0.5, alibi_slopes=None, output_scale=None,
+            sinks=None, causal=True)
+        return output
+
+    clean = attention()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(clean.double(), expected_output, atol=3e-4, rtol=3e-2)
+    value_cache[stale_page].fill_(float("nan"))
+    if nonfinite_keys:
+        key_cache[stale_page].fill_(float("nan"))
+    actual = attention()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual.double(), expected_output, atol=3e-4, rtol=3e-2)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, clean, atol=3e-4, rtol=3e-2)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("padded_layout", [False, True], ids=["native", "hybrid_stride"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("nonfinite_keys", [False, True], ids=["value_nan", "key_value_nan"])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_decode_sliding_window_ignores_expired_boundary_token(
+    padded_layout: bool, nonfinite_keys: bool,
+) -> None:
+    # An expired token in the first live page is still loaded when decode
+    # skips only whole expired tiles. Zero attention weight times NaN is NaN.
+    device = CUDA_DEVICES[0]
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device)
+    set_random_seed(46236)
+    batch, hq, hkv, dim, block, packing = 32, 16, 2, 128, 32, 8
+    seq_len, window = 4352, 4095
+    dtype = torch.bfloat16
+    query_lens = [1] * batch
+    dense_k = (torch.randn(batch, seq_len, hkv, dim, device=device) * 0.1).to(dtype)
+    dense_v = (torch.randn_like(dense_k, dtype=torch.float32) * 0.1).to(dtype)
+    query = (torch.randn(sum(query_lens), hq, dim, device=device) * 0.1).to(dtype)
+    key = torch.cat([dense_k[r, -n:] for r, n in enumerate(query_lens)])
+    value = torch.cat([dense_v[r, -n:] for r, n in enumerate(query_lens)])
+    starts = [0]
+    for n in query_lens:
+        starts.append(starts[-1] + n)
+    query_start_loc = torch.tensor(starts, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    seq_lens = torch.full((batch,), seq_len, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    pages_per_req = seq_len // block
+    table = torch.arange(1, batch * pages_per_req + 1, device=device,
+                         dtype=torch.int32).reshape(batch, pages_per_req)
+    num_pages = 1 + batch * pages_per_req
+    span = hkv * dim * block
+    stride = span * (2 if padded_layout else 1)
+    key_cache = torch.empty_strided(
+        (num_pages, hkv, dim // packing, block, packing),
+        (stride, dim * block, block * packing, packing, 1),
+        device=device, dtype=dtype)
+    value_cache = torch.empty_strided(
+        (num_pages, hkv, dim, block),
+        (stride, dim * block, block, 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)
+    key_cache[1:].copy_(
+        dense_k.reshape(batch, pages_per_req, block, hkv, dim)
+        .permute(0, 1, 3, 4, 2)
+        .reshape(batch * pages_per_req, hkv, dim // packing, packing, block)
+        .permute(0, 1, 2, 4, 3))
+    value_cache[1:].copy_(
+        dense_v.reshape(batch, pages_per_req, block, hkv, dim)
+        .permute(0, 1, 3, 4, 2)
+        .reshape(batch * pages_per_req, hkv, dim, block))
+    expired_token = seq_len - window - 1  # 256; first live token is 257.
+    boundary_pages = table[:, expired_token // block].long()
+    boundary_offset = expired_token % block
+    scale = torch.ones((), device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
+
+    expected = []
+    for req, n in enumerate(query_lens):
+        q64 = query[starts[req]:starts[req + 1]].double().transpose(0, 1)
+        k64 = dense_k[req].double().transpose(0, 1).repeat_interleave(hq // hkv, 0)
+        v64 = dense_v[req].double().transpose(0, 1).repeat_interleave(hq // hkv, 0)
+        # Reuse the existing explicit causal/window mask helper; FP64 matmul
+        # and softmax are independent of the kernel under test.
+        mask = create_causal_attention_mask_for_sdpa(
+            [n], [seq_len], sliding_window=window,
+            device=torch.device(device), dtype=torch.float64)
+        scores = (q64 @ k64.transpose(1, 2)) * dim ** -0.5 + mask
+        expected.append((scores.softmax(-1) @ v64).transpose(0, 1))
+    expected_output = torch.cat(expected)
+
+    def attention() -> torch.Tensor:
+        output = torch.empty_like(query)
+        chunked_prefill_paged_decode(
+            query=query, key=key, value=value, output=output,
+            kv_cache_dtype="auto", key_cache=key_cache, value_cache=value_cache,
+            block_table=table, query_start_loc=query_start_loc, seq_lens=seq_lens,
+            max_seq_len=seq_len, max_query_len=max(query_lens),
+            k_scale=scale, v_scale=scale, sliding_window=window,
+            sm_scale=dim ** -0.5, alibi_slopes=None, output_scale=None,
+            sinks=None, causal=True)
+        return output
+
+    clean = attention()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(clean.double(), expected_output, atol=3e-4, rtol=3e-2)
+    # Direct indexed assignment updates the cache, unlike fill_ on an
+    # advanced-indexing result, which would only mutate a temporary copy.
+    value_cache[boundary_pages, :, :, boundary_offset] = float("nan")
+    if nonfinite_keys:
+        key_cache[boundary_pages, :, :, boundary_offset, :] = float("nan")
+    actual = attention()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual.double(), expected_output, atol=3e-4, rtol=3e-2)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, clean, atol=3e-4, rtol=3e-2)
```
</details>

## Purpose

issue_comments.body:
Additional kernel-level evidence and a decode counterpart to this prefix repair. The duplicate check also found #49588, so I am sharing the patch here for coordination rather than opening a competing PR.

There is a remaining partial-tile case beyond skipping whole expired blocks. With `seq_len=4352`, `sliding_window=4095` and physical/kernel block size32, live keys start at257. Token256 is expired but shares the first retained tile with live token257. Poisoning only token256 still produces NaNs with #49588's loop-start change, because that token's K/V are loaded before the score mask. Extending the existing decode load predicate to the window boundary prevents this.

Focused pytest results on an allocated AMD GPU (BF16, PyTorch2.11.0+gitd0c8b1f, ROCm7.2.53211, Triton3.6.0):

| Decode implementation | Whole expired page (8 cases) | Expired token in first retained tile (4 cases) |
|---|---|---|
| Stock decode at this PR's `aa93f64c` head | 8 poisoned-output assertion failures | 4 poisoned-output assertion failures |
| Exact #49588 diff (`0b1ffc75`) on that same source | 8 passed | 4 poisoned-output assertion failures |
| Load-mask patch below | 8 passed | 4 passed |

Every variant passed the clean-input FP64 comparison before poisoning. The unchanged bound is `atol=3e-4, rtol=3e-2`. Cases cover ordinary and padded cache strides, V-only and K+V NaNs, and null/nonzero whole-page IDs. Boundary poisoning uses direct indexed assignment so it modifies the actual cache, not an advanced-indexing copy. Full upstream conftests remained enabled, and the exact imported kernel/test hashes and per-case JUnit outcomes were checked. This is focused Python-kernel coverage on an older installed vLLM runtime, not model-evaluation or throughput qualification.

Command for the appended tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py \
  -k 'decode_sliding_window_ignores_stale_nan_pages or decode_sliding_window_ignores_expired_boundary_token' \
  -q --junitxml=decode-window.xml
```

The decode patch preserves the no-window path and existing score semantics. It can coexist with #49588's whole-block skip; the combined implementation has not been tested in this run. The prefix implementation remains owned by this PR.

<details><summary>Decode load-mask patch</summary>

```diff
--- a/vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py
+++ b/vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py
@@ -185,8 +185,16 @@
         # use the cheaper token-uniform dim_mask (matching the pre-0.25.0 fast
         # path) and skip the per-token predicate entirely.
         # K : (HEAD_SIZE, BLOCK_SIZE), V : (BLOCK_SIZE, HEAD_SIZE)
-        if j == num_blocks - 1:
+        # Retired sliding-window entries may contain nonfinite values.
+        # Mask their loads: a zero attention weight does not neutralize NaN.
+        if j == num_blocks - 1 or (
+            SLIDING_WINDOW > 0 and start_n < seq_len - SLIDING_WINDOW
+        ):
             kv_load_mask = abs_token_idx < seq_len
+            if SLIDING_WINDOW > 0:
+                kv_load_mask = kv_load_mask & (
+                    (seq_len - 1 - abs_token_idx) < SLIDING_WINDOW
+                )
             K_load = tl.load(
                 key_cache_ptr + k_offset,
                 mask=dim_mask[:, None] & kv_load_mask[None, :],
```
</details>
